title: data_class.v1
description: The playbook's table of data classes (schemas/data_classes.v1.json; 00_UniversalStandards/16_Service_Design_Record.md §5). Each class states what losing or misreading its data costs, as requirements a store holding it must meet: how a write is acknowledged, how many copies exist and where, backup, consistency, which caching modes are allowed, and what a producer does when its buffer is full. Every store in a design record names one class. A strong class allows no replica reads and has a staleness bound of 0, and a quorum-acknowledged class keeps at least three synchronous copies. Class ids must be unique (relationship rule DR-018).

write_ack.description: When a write may be reported as done: never waited on, in memory, on disk, or on a quorum of replicas.

placement.description: The minimum spread of the copies; a store may exceed it.

replica_reads.description: Whether reads may be served from a replica or cache instead of the primary.

max_staleness_seconds.description: The longest a reader may see old data. Cache TTLs for this class may not exceed it.

caching.description: Caching modes allowed for this class; empty means none.

overflow.description: What a producer does when its buffer is full. Blocking a user's request is never allowed.
